title: Mass Gap of Four-Dimensional Lattice Yang–Mills Theory for Every Compact Simple Group
description: Three papers and a Lean 4/Mathlib certificate on four-dimensional lattice Yang–Mills theory, by Deep Bhattacharjee, Ushashi Bhattacharya, James Montgomery Lockwood and Tristan Romanov. (1) Spacing-Uniform Lattice Inequalities Cannot Produce the Yang–Mills Mass Gap: a lattice gap uniform in lattice units forces trivial continuum two-point functions. (2) Mass Gap of Lattice Yang–Mills Theory up to the Dobrushin Ceiling: the sharp Hessian bound 4d, the sharp quarter for von Mises–Fisher laws on the three-sphere, and a lattice mass gap for SU(2) up to beta_W = 2/9. (3) Mass Gap of Four-Dimensional Lattice Yang–Mills Theory for Every Compact Simple Group (Hexagon preprint 2610.00341). In a forest gauge, fixed on straight lines that meet each plaquette once: a unique state, reflection positivity, exponential clustering and a transfer-matrix gap for SU(2) up to beta_W = 0.345 and SU(3) up to beta_W = 0.76; for every compact simple group a gap for N|beta| < 2 kappa_G/29, with kappa_G the least Ricci curvature, extended to N|beta| < 2 kappa_G/28.840002 by T. Romanov's computer-assisted certificate (checked independently here and by J. M. Lockwood; its finite data are checked by the Lean 4 kernel). A conditional continuum step: a Dobrushin–Shlosman condition on one cube of fixed physical size, uniform along the tuning, gives a mass gap in physical units for every continuum limit. The paper shows what this condition needs and where it fails (large beta at a fixed cube size, the Gaussian field, U(1)), and builds a block-averaging route towards it: a constrained quadratic gap 537/5000 (Romanov's exact certificate), a covariant cut-off of Balaban's averaging that composes on fields of small curvature, chessboard bounds on large plaquettes under the SU(2) Wilson measure, and effective forms that are local uniformly in the scale. On the fibres of the cut-off average the constrained law is log-concave on a chart and its covariances decay exponentially with constants depending only on the group; every small-field point of a fibre lies in that chart, and the mass outside it is bounded in mean over the fibres (Theorem 123). Along its private links each cut-off average is a submersion with a constant independent of the field (Lemma 124), and for SU(2) its law under Haar measure has bounded density (Lemma 126), so a Peierls argument inside the fibre bounds the mass off the chart on every fibre through a field with small plaquettes (Proposition 127, Corollary 128); on every fibre, whatever the boundary links, the law concentrates near the least action of the fields whose averaging sites are near the identity (Lemma 129, Proposition 130, Corollary 131). Under the SU(2) Wilson measure, along logarithmic tuning, the fraction of bad unit cubes in a cube of fixed physical size is small with probability tending to one, uniformly over every exterior (Proposition 145). An appendix records two steps of arXiv:2606.19362 that fail as stated: a gap inferred from the two-point function of one observable, and a compactly supported spectral cutoff given a positive Laplace representation. Lean: 86 theorems and lemmas, no sorry, standard axioms only. The bound off the chart on fibres whose regular fields all have large action, the composition across scales and the existence of the continuum limit are not proved, so the continuum Yang–Mills existence and mass-gap problem remains open.
